mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate above 0.4 percentage points, sustained for two months, indicates a tightening labor market that increases wage pressures and input costs, which in turn compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of such unemployment rate declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, increasing real interest rates and eroding real corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 6-month moving averages indicates robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 6-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month average for six consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during six consecutive months of below-average housing starts.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in Real Personal Income (implied by RSAFS growth) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals strengthening household balance sheets and higher consumption potential, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 12-mo MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS growth exceeds its 12-month average for three consecutive months.
